verdict.rationale: Obsidian's docs say notes are stored locally as non-proprietary plain-text Markdown files, so you can switch to another app easily and edit them with other text editors. Leaving requires no export step, and community users confirm they own their files and that plain text can outlive Obsidian. Canvas uses JSON .canvas files, which is still an open format, and Wikilinks can be swapped for standard Markdown links for interoperability. Missing for 10: documented portability guidance for non-Markdown artifacts (Canvas, Bases views) and wikilink-heavy vaults when moving to other apps.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Obsidian uses non-proprietary plain text Markdown files stored locally on your device. You have total control over your data, which means you can use Obsidian offline and switch to another app easily
Because notes are plain text files, you can use other text editors and file managers to edit and manage notes.
If interoperability is important to you, you can disable Wikilinks and use Markdown links instead.
as plain text they can outlive Obsidian itself
